sam_customer: Hey — our production integration started returning 400s from /v1/generate when we enable JSON output mode. Happening ~11:22 UTC, request-id `req_0a1b2c3`. Example of the request body we send (redacted):

sam_customer: ```json
{
  "items": [
    { "item_id": "123", "text": "foo" },
    { "text": "bar", "temp_meta": { "source": "legacy" } },
    { "item_id": 125, "text": "baz" }
  ]
}
```

sam_customer: The second item has no `item_id` and also has an extra nested key `temp_meta`. Our downstream schema expects `item_id` required for every item (string).

maya_support: Thanks — sorry for the break. Can you confirm the exact API params you used (model + any `json_mode` / `response_format` flags) and whether you were streaming? Also can you paste the full `X-Request-ID` header value from your client?

sam_customer: We're calling `redwood-inference/v1/generate` with model `rw-instruct-v1.3` and the web client sets `format: json` (we don't stream). X-Request-ID was `req_0a1b2c3`. Full curl we used: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
-d @payload.json
```

maya_support: I escalated to eng. Alex, I attached the request-id. Logs show repeated parse failures for that req.

alex_eng: I pulled the trace for `req_0a1b2c3`. Verbose error is `JSONModeParserError: missing required field "item_id" at items[1]` thrown in the structured-output validator. Also saw that some of the `item_id` values are ints while others are strings — schema drift. We also logged `unrecognized key: temp_meta` in the nested object which is currently considered a hard failure for strict mode.

alex_eng: Quick notes:
- Validator is strict by default and rejects when required keys are missing or unknown keys are present in nested objects.
- This cluster has had a spike in client variants sending mixed types (int vs string) and some clients adding `temp_*` fields during A/B experiments.

alex_eng: Can you reproduce with the minimal payload? Try this and paste the response:```json
{
  "items": [
    { "item_id": "a", "text": "x" },
    { "text": "y" }
  ]
}
```

sam_customer: Reproduced locally with that minimal payload, same 400 and `missing required` error. We can't guarantee every client will always include `item_id` while we roll out a fix.

alex_eng: Okay — two potential short-term workarounds: 1) Ensure your producer adds `item_id` for all items (recommended), or 2) send a pre-validation pass on your side to fill defaults for missing `item_id`/normalize ints->strings.

maya_support: We're going to push a conservative tolerance change to avoid hard-failing when an optional nested key is present OR when the missing required field is clearly a customer schema mismatch that can be fallback-handled. Alex, can you scope?

alex_eng: I can implement a change: when `strict_structured_output=true`, we keep current behavior. When `strict_structured_output=false` (the fallback), the validator will: 1) coerce numeric ids to strings if schema expects string, 2) ignore unknown `temp_*` keys (log as warning), and 3) return a best-effort JSON output with diagnostics rather than a 400. I'll push to staging for QA.

tina_sre: Heads-up — we saw a small retry storm for this customer which caused a latency and cost bump. Billing alerted for unusual token usage (billing-bot: +7% spike). If we flip validator behavior we should avoid extra retries.

billing-bot: alert: account acct_987 increased token usage by 7% between 11:00-12:00 UTC due to 4xx retries. Billing team looped in.

maya_support: Timeline: Alex will deploy a non-breaking tolerant validator to staging within the hour and we will ask the customer to test. If staging looks good we'll rollout a limited prod canary for this customer only.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy to staging: tolerant-json-validator v0.3.1 — features: allow unknown nested keys (warn), coerce numeric id -> string, return diagnostics instead of 400.

alex_eng: Deployed to staging. SAM, can you re-run your failing payload against the staging endpoint? (staging api: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, same auth)

sam_customer: Tested on staging — the request now returns 200 and includes `diagnostics` with `missing_item_ids: [1]` and the `items[1].item_id` set to fallback "__generated_missing_id_1__". No 400s. Thanks! :raised_hands:

maya_support: Great — we'll schedule a small canary to the production shard that serves your account later today. We'll also follow up with a recommended client fix to always populate `item_id` and normalize types.

sam_customer: Appreciate the quick help. Can you please add a note to the ticket about potential billing credits for the retry spike? Our finance team will ask for that.

maya_support: Will do — looping in billing and support docs update.

alex_eng: Follow-ups for us: add telemetry to detect `mixed-id-types` and `unknown-nested-keys` spikes, make validator mode configurable per-customer, and update docs with best practices for structured JSON mode.

tina_sre: I'll create the SLO postmortem notes and retention for the logs — flagging for oncall review.

maya_support: Closing loop once production canary is healthy and billing team confirms any credits. Thanks all.

sam_customer: Confirmed production canary fixed the issue for our live traffic at 12:45 UTC. No further 400s.

maya_support: Marking resolved for now. If the issue resurfaces please re-open with `X-Request-ID`. :white_check_mark:
